hints: Focus on how an ester is made, a carboxylic acid plus an alcohol with water removed, so try splitting the ester back apart.
Notice the left side is $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2$, which comes from the simple 2-carbon acid $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$.
Look at the O-CH2 bond on the right side and rebuild the alcohol as HO-CH2 with the methyl branch kept in exactly the same position.
walkthrough:
**Recall how esters form**

Esters are made by esterification of a carboxylic acid and an alcohol with concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst and heat.

$$\text{carboxylic acid} + \text{alcohol} \rightleftharpoons \text{ester} + \text{water}$$

**Split the ester at the COO link**

Think of the ester as acid part plus alcohol part joined at the $\text{CO}_2$ group. The $\text{C=O}$ side belongs to the acid, the $\text{O-C}$ side belongs to the alcohol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H} + \text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Identify the two reactants**

The left fragment gives ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. The right fragment gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, which is 2-methylbutan-1-ol.

This matches the pair of ethanoic acid plus 2-methylbutan-1-ol, which forms the banana odour ester.

options.A: This swaps the roles. It uses methanol as the alcohol and a branched 5-carbon acid. That would give a methyl ester, $\text{...CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, not an ester with $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2$ on the left and a branched 5-carbon O-alkyl group on the right.
options.B: This uses ethanol as the alcohol and a branched 4-carbon acid. That would give an ethyl ester, $\text{...CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, with the branch on the acid side. Our target has the branch on the alcohol side and ethanoate on the acid side.
options.C: Ethanoic acid $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ provides the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2$ part, and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ provides the $\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ part. Together with loss of water they give exactly the target ester.
options.D: The acid is correct, but the alcohol is the wrong isomer. This is 3-methylbutan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, with the methyl on carbon 3 from the OH end. The target needs the methyl on carbon 2, as in 2-methylbutan-1-ol.
